5 ترضّح (S, K) and ↓ ارتضح (L) It (a pebble, S, K, and a date-stone, L, K) became broken, (S, L, K,) [or bruised, brayed, or crushed,] with a stone [&c.]. (L.) Jirán-el-' Owd says, “يَكَادُ الحَصَى مِنْ وَطْئِهَا يَتَرَضَّحُ
” [The pebbles almost became broken by her tread]. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
